newsitem.title: INDIA: Police detain Kashmiri separatist leader.
newsitem.headline: Police detain Kashmiri separatist leader.

text.p: Indian police on Friday detained a senior Shia Moslem separatist leader who violated a ban on public gatherings and led a religious procession through troubled Kashmir's largest city, police said.

They said Moulana Abbass Ansari, an executive member of Kashmir's leading separatist alliance, the All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference, was detained along with a dozen supporters in the heart of Srinagar.
Ansari is also one of the chief priests of Shia Moslems in Jammu and Kashmir, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem-majority state. Srinagar is the Himalayan province's summer capital.
Police used tear gas and batons to disperse Moharram processions at several places in Srinagar, witnesses said.
Shia Moslems mourn the slaying of a grandson of Prophet Mohammad during the first Islamic month of Moharram.

A Hurriyat spokesman said Ansari was injured when police used batons to disperse the procession. "We strongly condemn use of force by Indian authorities on a religous procession," Hurriyat chairman Umar Farooq said.
A police spokesman said the procession had violated orders that ban public gatherings of more than four people on the grounds that they may pose a threat to law and order.
More than 20,000 people have been killed in the Kashmir Valley since a separatist rebellion broke out in 1990, according to police and hospitals.
Shops and schools in Srinagar remained closed for a fifth day on Friday in response to a strike called by the separatists, protesting against alleged human rights violations by Indian troops.
Indian authorities deny charges of gross human rights abuses and say they investigate all rights violation allegations and punish soldiers who are found guilty.
